data.body:
Root cause. `services/orchestration/intake_reconciler.py:397` built the `intake_start` ledger target from a content digest of the ticket. ADP writes comments and status changes back during a run, which changes the digest. A later watermark poll computed a different target, missed the completed ledger row, and admitted a duplicate run once the prior execution reached a terminal state. The fix keys the target on `{issue_key}:{repo}`.

Interaction with ADEVX-140. Before ADEVX-140, a lingering `PR_CREATED` execution row blocked re-admission by accident. ADEVX-140 makes a finished run reach `COMPLETED` immediately, which removes that accidental block. This dedup key is now the only guard against a duplicate run on the intake path.

Defects found in code review and fixed before merge.
1. The first implementation of the legacy-compatibility layer made the ledger insert conditional on no legacy match. When a legacy row matched with status `pending`, no row was inserted under the new key, `run_once` saw `replayed=False` and started the workflow, then `record` updated by the new key and affected zero rows. Every poll would have started a duplicate run forever. The insert is now unconditional with `on_conflict_do_nothing`, matching the original structure.
2. The legacy lookup used `target.like(f"%:{repo}")`, which interpolates the repository name into a LIKE pattern where `_` and `%` are wildcards. Rows are now fetched by task id, execution id, and operation, then filtered on a literal parsed repository suffix in Python.

Advisories investigated and fixed.
- A redundant unreachable branch was removed.
- A dead `target_1` check in the test double was removed.
- Postgres-ledger coverage was added for the legacy-completed replay branch that protects the existing rows.
- In-memory ledger coverage was added for reentry detection against a pending legacy record.
- Postgres ledger coverage was added for reentry detection against a pending legacy row.
- The ledger test double now honours `order_by(updated_at.desc())`, and a test proves the most recently updated legacy row decides the replay.

Advisory investigated and declined. Code review noted that a matched legacy pending row is left in the database with status `pending` after the current key completes. It is inert. A later `reserve` of the current key matches the completed row on the exact-key lookup, which short-circuits before the legacy fallback. `services/orchestration/intake_retry.py:121-127` deletes both rows on the operator re-run path.

Falsification. Reverting the unconditional insert to the conditional form fails `legacy_pending_intake_start_is_completed_under_the_current_key`. Reverting the in-memory pending lookup to an exact-key check fails `pending_legacy_intake_start_makes_the_current_key_reentrant`. Dropping `reentrant=existing is not None` fails `pending_legacy_intake_start_row_makes_the_current_key_reentrant`. Dropping the `order_by` clause fails `the_most_recently_updated_legacy_intake_start_row_wins`.

Evidence. Ledger state before the change showed 17 `intake_start` rows, all `completed`, none `pending`, which is why the compatibility layer was kept rather than deleted. Without it all 17 tickets become re-admittable.

Gates. `inv ci` at `47de6c3`: 1474 passed, 6 skipped, eval-gate PASS, exit 0. All 14 acceptance-criteria selectors proven individually. Plan review PASS. Code review PASS at `47de6c3`, 0 blocking, 0 advisory.

Follow-up worth ticketing. `services/orchestration/intake_retry.py:125` still matches with `target.like(f"%:{repo}")`, so a repository name containing an underscore can over-match on the operator clear path.
